note: ONE MAN, TWO MARRIAGES, TWO COMUNI. Son of Nicotra D. Giuseppe and Caltabiano D. Gioachina. Married Angela Ligresti at RIPOSTO on 23 April 1838 (Matrimoni atto 15) and Antonina Consoli at GIARRE on 19 August 1844 (Matrimoni atto 54) — the two acts name the same two parents, which is what joins them. Children Salvatore in November 1846 and Salvatore again in January 1848. AND HIS OWN PATRIA IS WRITTEN DIFFERENTLY IN THE TWO REGISTERS: «S. Giovanni» at Riposto, «Giarre» at Giarre

THREE children at Mascali, not two: Venera 11 May 1840 (atto 33), GIUSEPPE 19 MAY 1842 (atto 20) and Maria 1847 (atto 69). Giuseppe was found only on the 7 October 2026 re-read — the original sweep cleared 1842 at the M-to-next-letter junction and never saw the N section, which is exactly the failure work-list row 180 was raised for
not seen in a register of their own — named as the GIARRE-born groom's parents in Riposto Matrimoni 1844 atto 39. The first ordinary, untitled Nicotra household this archive can put at Giarre
Nicotra Rosaria, atto 198, 13 April 1820 — in the first year Giarre registered anything

Nicotra Carmela, atto 228, 1 May 1820. THE NAME IS RIGHT AND THE GENERATION IS NOT: Giovanni's father Rosario was a bracciante still working in 1872, and a man fathering a child in 1820 would be past seventy-five by then. A grandfather-generation namesake is exactly what Sicilian naming custom predicts, and custom is not a document

named as the parents of NICOTRA ALFIO, who married Venera Cesaro at Giarre on 9 January 1838 (Matrimoni atto 2). Set beside Riposto Matrimoni 1844 — Nicotra Salvadore, patria GIARRE, son of NICOTRA ALFIO and Rosa Pappalardo — the two acts give an ALTERNATING ALFIO/SALVADORE descent at Giarre across three generations, which is exactly what Sicilian naming custom produces. NOT JOINED: the two mothers are both a Rosa and neither surname matches, and custom is not a document

Nicotra Catarina, atto 58, 12 February 1821. A SECOND Salvadore Nicotra at Giarre, and NOT obviously the one named in Matrimoni 1838 — that act makes Nicotra Alfio the son of Nicotra Salvadore and LA SPINA ROSA, not Costa Anna. One man remarried, or two men of one name. Not decided

Nicotra Giuseppe, atto 191, May 1821. AND THIS MAY BE THE 1820 ROSARIO UNDER A DIFFERENT WIFE'S NAME, OR A MISREADING OF MINE: the 1820 entry was read as NICOTRA ROSARIO and ROSA PROVIDENZA, this one as PAOLA PREVITERA. Providenza and Previtera are a plausible slip for each other; Rosa and Paola are not. One of the two readings is probably wrong and I have not established which — the acts themselves would settle it

SEVEN NICOTRA DEATHS in nine years of Mascali's death indexes: ORAZIA 1875/107, MARIA 1876/14, GIUSEPPE 1879/21, SALVATORE 1880/63, LEONARDO 1880/95, NUNZIATO 1881/2, SALVATORE 1881/14. NONE IS ROSARIO AND NONE IS VENERA MURABITO. BOTH CANDIDATES WERE TESTED BY FETCHING THE ACTS. The 1879 GIUSEPPE IS DISPROVED: he died aged ONE YEAR, son of Venero Nicotra and Venera Sorbello, not the Giuseppe born 19 May 1842. The 1876 MARIA CANNOT BE READ: her act lies under the archive's own black cover sheet

A BRACCIALE NICOTRA HOUSEHOLD AT MASCALI — the social condition Rosario Nicotra shares, and the first of its kind found here. Named in Morti 1879 atto 21, the death of their son GIUSEPPE aged ONE YEAR on 3 April 1879. Nothing attaches them to Rosario and nothing should until an act does. A SECOND CHILD LOST: Morti 1883 atto 10, ANGELA aged EIGHT MONTHS, died 23 January 1883 at contrada Costaporane, so born about May 1882. TWO INFANTS IN FOUR YEARS.
AND THE MOTHER'S FORENAME DOES NOT MATCH. The 1879 act was read here as VENERA Sorbello; the 1883 act says SEBASTIANA SORBELLO, in a clean hand. Same surname, same trade, same comune, four years apart — so either one reading is wrong, or Venero remarried a second Sorbello, or the woman carried both names. It is recorded as a disagreement and NOT resolved: the 1879 act should be re-read at full width before anybody decides.

Forty years old, lavorante, of Mascali, and the witness GIOVANNI NICOTRA CHOSE HIMSELF for his daughter's birth act of 13 December 1873 — «testimoni scelti dal dichiarante stesso». A man picks his own witnesses, so this is the nearest thing to a kinsman the record offers, and it is still not a join. The 1873 index has him fathering a son Giovanni at act 31. His own father ANGELO was dead by 1873.

Of NUNZIATA, in the comune of Mascali. Forty-three and a lavorante in January 1877, so born about 1833. Two daughters in the index: MARIA, 28 March 1874 (act 47, paternità Gaetano), and ROSARIA, born 7 January 1877 at half past seven in the morning (act 8, read in the original). HIS DAUGHTER MARIA IS THE NAMESAKE TRAP: the archive's own Maria Nicotra was born to GIOVANNI at Mascali on 8 December 1875, twenty months later. Two Maria Nicotras, one town, one decade, different fathers.

NOT A NICOTRA HOUSEHOLD, and it is here because half the name this archive is looking for is MURABITO. Three children in the Giarre birth Tavole: VENERA 1827 act 98, SERAFINA 1828 act 158, SALVADORE 1832 act 155. Settled at Giarre across six years rather than passing through. The forenames are what matter: on Sicilian custom a first daughter carries the paternal grandmother's name and a first son the paternal grandfather's, so this household points back to a SALVADORE MURABITO and a VENERA. Their own Venera, born 1827, is NOT Rosario Nicotra's wife — she would have been fourteen when Giovanni was born about 1841 — but a Venera Murabito of the right generation would be Giuseppe's sister or cousin, and this is the family to test that against.

Son ROSARIO, act 100 of 1834. A DIFFERENT WIFE from the Coppolino Agostina household, so either a second man of the name or a remarriage — Giarre is the largest comune in this archive and more than one Giuseppe Murabito is ordinary. Noted because the wife is a VENERA and the son a ROSARIO, which are the two forenames of the couple this archive cannot find. Wrong surname for the wife and far too late for the son, and it is a coincidence, not a lead.

Daughter VENERA, act 203 of 1836. A THIRD wife recorded against the name Giuseppe Murabito at Giarre, and the SECOND daughter called Venera among the Giarre Murabito. That is the finding worth carrying: VENERA IS A RECURRING MURABITO FORENAME HERE, so «Venera Murabito» in the 1872 act is an ordinary Giarre name and cannot be pinned to a household on the name alone.
Three children across nine years: ANGELA 1828 act 91 (the surname spelled Bertagallo there), ROSARIO 1835 act 134, ANGELO 1837 act 146. Settled at Giarre.
Daughter ANGELA, act 83 of 1828 — one of two girls called Angela born to different Murabito parents in the same year, which is how the households are told apart.

Son SALVADORE, act 45 of 1835. An ALFIO Murabito at Giarre — Alfio is the forename this archive has been following through the NICOTRA of Giarre and Riposto, and here it is in the other surname. Recorded, not joined.

THE TITLED LINE, AND THE FIRST MARRIAGE THIS ARCHIVE HAS FOR ANY NICOTRA. Their son D. FRANCESCO NICOTRA, twenty-five and a CALZOLAJO, born and living at Giarre, married Maria Sapienza of Riposto there on 14 June 1830 — Riposto Matrimoni 1830 atto 12, read in the original. Rosaria Misano was SIXTY-FOUR in 1830, so born about 1766, which puts this couple's own marriage in the 1790s and makes them the earliest Nicotra generation the archive has reached anywhere. The «D.» is Don on both father and son. THIS IS NOT ROSARIO'S FAMILY: Rosario Nicotra is a bracciante and his son Giovanni a lavorante, and nothing connects a labouring household at Mascali to a titled artisan one at Giarre except a surname and a town. It is filed so that the next person meeting a Giarre Nicotra knows which family they have.

A THIRD LABOURING NICOTRA HOUSEHOLD AT MASCALI, from Morti 1883 atto 10's neighbour: atto 123, MARIA aged TWO, died 16 December 1883 at contrada Cava, so born about 1881. Both parents braccianti.
WHETHER THIS IS THE GIUSEPPE THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HAS IS NOT SETTLED. GIUSEPPE NICOTRA FU ANGELO, forty and a lavorante, is the witness Giovanni Nicotra chose himself for his daughter's birth in 1873 — he would be about fifty here, which is late but possible for a two-year-old's father. The 1873 act gives no wife, so there is nothing to match VENERA COCO against. Two Giuseppe Nicotra at Mascali is equally possible and the archive does not pick.

THE FIRST MURABITO AT MASCALI, and the only one outside Giarre. Mascali Morti 1885 atto 4, read in the original: a BRACCIALE, BORN AT MASCALI, son of the late PAOLO MURABITO, WIDOWER of FRANCESCA PARISI, died 13 January 1885 and declared to be ONE HUNDRED AND SIX.
WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS NOT A JOIN. This archive is looking for VENERA MURABITO, wife of a bracciante, living at Mascali in 1872. Until now every Murabito it had was at Giarre and none was a labourer. Here is a labouring Murabito family native to Mascali, with a PAOLO a generation above Bartolo. Nothing in the act names Venera, and nothing should be claimed. The age must not be taken as written either: a declared 106 is the classic inflation, and this archive's audit records ages running out by one to four years as routine. Even at eighty he is of the generation that could father a Venera born about 1815-1825.

THE EARLIEST NICOTRA HOUSEHOLD AT MASCALI. Their son ALFIO married CARMELA SUDIERI on 3 November 1831 — Mascali Matrimoni 1831 atto 18, the first Nicotra groom found in any Mascali marriage Tavola. The index gives his PATRIA as MASCALI, so this family was settled here by about 1805 and did not come from Giarre.
NOT ROSARIO'S PARENTS. Rosario Nicotra's death act of 1890 names his father as SIMONE and his mother as MARIANNA MUSUMECI, and says he was born at GIARRE. Two different Nicotra families at Mascali, one native and one that arrived from Giarre. The ALFIO is worth carrying: an Alfio Nicotra fathers a child at Mascali in 1873, and whether that is this man at about sixty-five or a son named for him is not settled.
